subject: literature
passage: For eleven years the Vidal sisters had run the bakery on Calle Ombú together, and for eleven years they had quarreled over their mother's recipe for anise bread: Inés wanted a slower rise, while Paloma swore by an extra spoonful of honey. So when a reporter from the neighborhood paper asked which of them deserved credit for the loaf that had made the shop famous, Inés braced herself for an argument. Paloma only brushed the flour from her apron. "Neither of us," she said. "The credit belongs to our mother, who taught Inés and ______ everything we know about bread."
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: Inside the quotation, the blank is part of a compound object of the verb "taught": the mother taught "Inés and ______." Test it by dropping "Inés and": the mother taught "me," not "I." An object takes the object pronoun "me."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Mine" is a possessive pronoun meaning "the one belonging to me"; "taught Inés and mine" doesn't name a person who was taught.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "I" is a subject pronoun; you wouldn't say "who taught I everything," so it can't be the object of "taught."
explanation.C: Incorrect. A reflexive pronoun such as "myself" needs an antecedent in the same clause; the subject of "taught" is "who" (the mother), so "myself" has nothing to refer back to.
explanation.D: Correct. The object pronoun "me" is correct as part of the compound object of "taught."
